info.title: EP-POM-CCTI
info.description:
This API defines the template end-points for the payment requests, responses and notifications between channels, bank origination systems and backoffice execution systems using the canonical representation of FIS Enterprise Payment semantics, commonly referred to as Universal Execution API. It also defines template end-points for the operations supported to help channels construct payment requests and obtain indicative processing information using the canonical representation of FIS Enterprise Payment semantics prior to execution.

When implemented by FIS Enterprise Payments products, this template will be used to generate one or more end-point definitions, defined by the roles of the actors participating in the interface.

__$ACTOR_ROLE__ denotes the component (either FIS or the customer) that is implementing the API end-points (for example, "POMBULK_CT ORM Application", "POMBULK_CT ORM Consumer", "POMBULK_CT Execution System")  
__$FUNCTIONALITY__ describes the behaviour of the of interaction, for example "Origination", "Clearing".

Sample titles based on the above examples would be
* Enterprise Payments: Universal Execution Origination (POMBULK_CT ORM Application)
* Enterprise Payments: Universal Execution Origination (POMBULK_CT ORM Consumer)
* Enterprise Payments: Universal Execution Clearing (POMBULK_CT Execution System)
* Enterprise Payments: Universal Execution Clearing (POMBULK_CT ORM Application)

For explanation on which actor needs to implement which end-point, refer to the FIS EP Universal Execution MUG documentation.

parameters.name: uuid
parameters.description: This header parameter identifies an API interaction. It must be provided in every request and is echoed in each 2xx response ??? and can also be echoed in the HTTP 4xx and 5xx responses in case of errors being returned by the server. The value must be a uuid.

parameters.name: organization-id
parameters.description: FIS processing organization ID - the fe/orgId the consumer is focused upon

parameters.name: idempotency-key
parameters.description: This header parameter represents an idempotency key for a POST API interaction. It must be provided in every request and have the same value in case of an idempotent retry.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: An optional header, environment, is introduced to support multi-environment routing for the same API. This header is used by the gateway to dynamically resolve the target backend endpoint during request processing. When the environment header is not present or contains the value 2 the request is routed to the primary endpoint (EP) as defined in the endpoint configuration.

businessProcessingDate.description: Processing date and time indicated by the sender for the receiver of the business message. This date may be different from the date and time provided in the CreationDate. Usage: Market practice or bilateral agreement should specify how this element should be used.

copyDuplicate.description:
Indicates whether the message is a Copy, a Duplicate or a copy of a duplicate of a previously sent ISO 20022 Message. Flag indicating if the Business Message exchanged between the MessagingEndpoints is possibly a duplicate.  If the receiving MessagingEndpoint did not receive the original, then this Business Message should be processed as if it were the original.  The possible values are:
- CODU: CopyDuplicate. Message is being sent as a copy to a party other than the account owner, for information purposes and the message is a duplicate of a message previously sent.
- COPY: Copy. Message is being sent as a copy to a party other than the account owner, for information purposes.
- DUPL: Duplicate. Message is for information/confirmation purposes. It is a duplicate of a message previously sent.

possibleDuplicate.description: If the receiving MessagingEndpoint did receive the original, then it should perform necessary actions to avoid processing this Business Message again. This will guarantee business idempotent behaviour. Note: this is named 'PossResend' in FIX. This is an application level resend not a network level retransmission.

priority.description: Relative indication of the processing precedence of the message over a (set of) Business Messages with assigned priorities.

BusinessApplicationHeaderV02.description: The Business Layer deals with Business Messages. The behaviour of the Business Messages is fully described by the Business Transaction and the structure of the Business Messages is fully described by the Message Definitions and related Message Rules, Rules and Market Practices. All of which are registered in the ISO 20022 Repository. A single new Business Message (with its accompagnying business application header) is created - by the sending MessagingEndpoint - for each business event; that is each interaction in a Business Transaction.

- DEBT: BorneByDebtor. All transaction charges are to be borne by the debtor.
- CRED: BorneByCreditor.All transaction charges are to be borne by the creditor
- SHAR: Shared. In a credit transfer context, means that transaction charges on the sender side are to be borne by the debtor, transaction charges on the receiver side are to be borne by the creditor. In a direct debit context, means that transaction charges on the sender side are to be borne by the creditor, transaction charges on the receiver side are to be borne by the debtor.
- SLEV: FollowingServiceLevel. Charges are to be applied following the rules agreed in the service level and/or scheme.

chequeType.description:
Specifies the type of cheque to be issued. The possible values are:
- CCHQ: CustomerCheque. Cheque drawn on the account of the debtor, and debited on the debtor's account when the cheque is cashed. Synonym is 'corporate cheque'.
- CCCH: CertifiedCustomerCheque. Cheque drawn on the account of the debtor, and debited on the debtor's account when the cheque is cashed. The financial institution prints and certifies the cheque, guaranteeing the payment.
- BCHQ: BankCheque. Cheque drawn on the account of the debtor's financial institution, which is debited on the debtor's account when the cheque is issued.These cheques are printed by the debtor's financial institution and payment is guaranteed by the financial institution. Synonym is 'cashier's cheque'.
- DRFT: Draft. A guaranteed bank cheque with a future value date (do not pay before], which in commercial terms is a 'negotiatable instrument': the beneficiary can receive early payment from any bank under subtraction of a discount. The ordering customer's account is debited on value date.
- ELDR: ElectronicDraft. An instrument with a future value date (do not pay before], which in commercial terms is a 'negotiatable instrument': the beneficiary can receive early payment from any bank under subtraction of a discount. The ordering customer's account is debited on value date.

paymentInformationIdentification.description: Unique identification, as assigned by a sending party, to unambiguously identify the payment information group within the message.

instructionIdentification.description: Unique identification, as assigned by an instructing party for an instructed party, to unambiguously identify the instruction. Usage: The instruction identification is a point to point reference that can be used between the instructing party and the instructed party to refer to the individual instruction. It can be included in several messages related to the instruction.

endToEndIdentification.description: Unique identification, as assigned by the initiating party, to unambiguously identify the transaction. This identification is passed on, unchanged, throughout the entire end-to-end chain. Usage: The end-to-end identification can be used for reconciliation or to link tasks relating to the transaction. It can be included in several messages related to the transaction. Usage: In case there are technical limitations to pass on multiple references, the end-to-end identification must be passed on throughout the entire end-to-end chain.

transactionIdentification.description: Unique identification, as assigned by the first instructing agent, to unambiguously identify the transaction that is passed on, unchanged, throughout the entire interbank chain. Usage: The transaction identification can be used for reconciliation, tracking or to link tasks relating to the transaction on the interbank level. Usage: The instructing agent has to make sure that the transaction identification is unique for a pre-agreed period.

mandateIdentification.description: Unique identification, as assigned by the creditor, to unambiguously identify the mandate.

chequeNumber.description: Unique and unambiguous identifier for a cheque as assigned by the agent.

clearingSystemReference.description: Unique reference, as assigned by a clearing system, to unambiguously identify the instruction. Usage: In case there are technical limitations to pass on multiple references, the end-to-end identification must be passed on throughout the entire end-to-end chain.

accountOwnerTransactionIdentification.description: Unambiguous identification of the securities transaction as known by the securities account owner (or the instructing party managing the account).

accountServicerTransactionIdentification.description: Unambiguous identification of the securities transaction as known by the securities account servicer.

marketInfrastructureTransactionIdentific.description: Identification of a securities transaction assigned by a market infrastructure other than a central securities depository, for example, Target2-Securities.

processingIdentification.description: Identification of the securities transaction assigned by the processor of the instruction other than the securities account owner, the securities account servicer and the market infrastructure.

proprietary.description: proprietary

uUIDIdentifier.description: Universally Unique IDentifier (UUID) version 4, as described in IETC RFC 4122 Universally Unique IDentifier (UUID) URN Namespace.

type.description: Identifies the type of reference reported.

reference.description: Proprietary reference specification related to the underlying transaction.

ProprietaryReference.description: Set of elements to identify a proprietary reference.

adviceTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system.

firstInstructionTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system, the current FI or the initiating channel/vendor.

firstMessageTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system, the current FI or the initiating channel/vendor.

internalMessageTraceIdentification.description: Generated by a FIS system, used for batch sumission across FIS systems only.

transactionTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system, the current FI or the initiating channel/vendor.

TaskExpiry.description: Defines the expiry date and time for a task.

DateAndDateTimeChoice.description: Choice between a date or a date and time format.

placeAndName.description: Unambiguous reference to the location where the supplementary data must be inserted in the message instance. In the case of XML, this is expressed by a valid XPath. In the case of JSON, this is expressed as a valid absolute JSON path starting with $ as the root node and using 0-based indexes when applicable.

SupplementaryData1CustomerCreditTransfer.description: Additional information that can not be captured in the structured fields and/or any other specific block.
Technical component that contains the validated supplementary data information. This technical envelope allows to segregate the supplementary data information from any other information.

forceFunds.description: Flag to force DR posting (originating leg), when the account has insufficient funds.

firstInstructionReceiptIdentification.description: Reference number given to a human user who originates an outbound payment.

firstInstructionTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system, the current FI or the initiating channel/vendor.

Pain001v11UniversalPaymentInformationSup.description: Supplementary Data provided at Payment Information level.

interactionMethod.description: Identifies how the payment is created in the channel (e.g. reading QR-code or BAR-code, manual input, payment is copied, generated by Bank application, data from somewhere else.

sagaId.description: A unique identifier for the logical thread of execution represented by a sequence of one or more API invocations.

schema.description:
URI of the schema describing the structure data information contained in the component. The possible values are:
- urn:fis:ep:common:client_context:1:

ClientContext.description: Information about the end-user that is performing the request.

staffFlag.description: Staff Flag. Indicates if the user is a company/bank staff one, or a customer.

userIdType.description: Indicates the type of identifier provided for User Id (email, SSN, national id number, self-service id, etc).

name.description: The name of the application that triggered the request.

path.description: The external logical endpoint (eg. Virtual Directory) on which the executing request was received.

serverName.description: The server machine name that is executing the request.

serverPort.description: The port that the host is serving against.

Application.description: Information about the application triggering the request.

CustomerInformationChoice.description: Specifies the customer information. Either a list of generic identifications, or the FIS EP standard customer information.

componentType.description: The kind of device used (mobile phone, ATM, Kiosk, Wearable device, etc).

manufacturerId.description: Identification of the software, hardware or system provider of the device.

modelId.description: Identification of a model of device for a given manufacturer.

modelName.description: Name of a model of device for a given manufacturer.

cookies.description: The http cookies that were sent in the request.

headers.description: The http headers that were sent in the request.

httpMethod.description: The http request method used. Ie GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH.

securityToken.description: Security token provided by the channel. It verifies the authentication and authorization for the executed action.

sessionId.description: The request session Id, is a unique identifier assigned to the Session at the at the instant an end-user commences a new session with an application.

uri.description: The full path, exclusive of host name and query string parameters, that was utilised to access the currently executing API.

url.description: The full URL, inclusive of host name and query string parameters, that was utilised to access the currently executing API.

userAgent.description: The user agent of the calling application.

userHostAddress.description: The ip address of the client that initiated the request.

coordinates.description: Representation of the geographical location in a specific format or positioning system. For example, 38.959390,-95.265483 for Decimal Degrees.

formatSystem.description: Format for reporting the location. Typical formats are DD (Decimal Degrees), DMS (Degrees, Minutes, Seconds), DDM (Degrees and Decimal Minutes), and UTM (Universal Transverse Mercator). Other formats can be used as well.

GeographicLocation.description: Geographic location on the Earth specified in a given calculation system.

items.description: Set of closed user groups that identify pre-agreed banking practices that apply to this account.

CashAccountInformation.description: Set of elements used to supplement debtor account information with banking practices, closed user groups, etc.

PaymentInformationServicesExecutions.description: Specifies details of the executed services at instruction level.

completed.description: This is the flag to indicate the completion of the service execution.

AccountingServiceExecutionInformation.description: Information about the execution of the accounting service.

completed.description: Completed flag. Should only be set if a full FX has occurred and source and target amounts are provided

ForeignExchangeServiceExecutionInformati.description: Specifies details of the executed foreign exchange service.

CurrencyAndAmountExchange.description: Specifies details of the currency and amount within an FX quote.

rateType.description:
Specifies the type used to complete the currency exchange. The possible values are:
- SPOT: Spot. Exchange rate applied is the spot rate.
- SALE: Sale. Exchange rate applied is the market rate at the time of the sale.
- AGRD: Agreed. Exchange rate applied is the rate agreed between the parties.

contractIdentification.description: Unique and unambiguous reference to the foreign exchange contract agreed between the initiating party/creditor and the debtor agent.

ExchangeRate.description: Further detailed information on the exchange rate that has been used in the payment transaction.

BaseOneRate.description: Rate expressed as a decimal, for example, 0.7 is 7/10 and 70%.

CurrencyAndAmount.description: A number of monetary units specified in an active or a historic currency where the unit of currency is explicit and compliant with ISO 4217.

quoteIdentification.description: Reference to identify a FX quote

QuoteExecutionInformation.description: Specifies details of the executed FX quote.

FundsReservationServiceExecutionInformat.description: Specifies details of the executed funds reservation service.

coreBankingReferenceIdentification.description: Core banking reference for the funds reservation.

externalReferenceIdentification.description: External reference to the funds reservation, as generated by the payment system that created the reservation.

FundsReservationExecutionInformation.description: Specifies details of the executed funds reservation.

identification.description: Standing Order Identification provided by the Standing Order Management application during the generation of the payment.

StandingOrderInformation.description: Specifies details provided by the Standing Order Management application during the generation of the payment.

URI of the schema describing the supplementary data information contained in this Envelope. The root property of this supplementary data information must be located next to this Schema property. The possible values are:

channelType.description:
Channel type. Provides detailed information on the canonical channel type codes. See FIS EP External Code Sets (ChannelTypeCode) document for more information about allowed values. The possible values are:
- DFLT: Default value (Single channel).
- IWEB: Online/Internet Banking.
- IMOB: Mobile Banking.
- TELE: Phone Banking.
- BRNC: Branch.
- BATM: Kiosk/ATM.
- CORP: Corporate.
- CASH: Cash Management.
- TREA: Treasury.
- GTWY: Gateway (SWIFT, PAG, etc).

firstMessageTraceIdentification.description: Generated by the first FIS system, the current FI or the initiating channel/vendor.

Pain001v11UniversalMessageSupplement1.description: Supplementary Data provided at Message level.

type.description: (Optional) An URI that identifies the type of error condition that occurred. The value of type may be represented as a URL that resolves to an HTML representation of a description of the type, or a URN. Type values should be unique within the the broadest practical namespace.

title.description: (Optional) An URI that identifies the type of error condition that occurred. The value of type may be represented as a URL that resolves to an HTML representation of a description of the type, or a URN. Type values should be unique within the the broadest practical namespace.

ErrorResponse.description: Error response body. The structure is compliant with FIS Code:Connect.

code.description: (Required) a unique code, meant to identify the error that occurred. This code is purely symbolic, i.e. its value is arbitrarily chosen to represent a given error and should not reveal underlying aspects of the API system.

message.description: (Required) a corresponding message that describes the error that occurs and how to solve it

items.description: (Optional*) A list of fields may be used to identify a set of particular attributes of an API request that is in error. Not to be used alongside 'field'

ErrorResponseDetails.description: Error response details. The structure is compliant with FIS Code:Connect.

reason.reasonDescription: Not allowed Business Application Header field

uuid.description: This header parameter identifies an API interaction. It must be provided in every request and is echoed in each 2xx response. The value must be a uuid.

Content-Type.description: Identifies the MIME type of the message body. API message senders and receivers can assume that charset, if not specified, is UTF-8.

Strict-Transport-Security.description: A header to indicate to browsers that the API must be accessed secure (HTTPS).

X-XSS-Protection.description: A header to stop pages from loading when reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks are detected. Mandadory value: 1;mode=block
